findings.body:
The `None` arm of `rfind(' ')` in `shorten` is never exercised. Every test input has a space within the first `limit` characters, so the branch that returns `format!("{head}…")` for an unbroken run of characters (e.g. a long single token) could be changed or broken without a test going red.

```rust
        Some(space) => format!("{}…", &head[..space]),
        None => format!("{head}…"),
```
findings.title: Cover the no-space branch of shorten

findings.body:
The `None` arm of `first_sentence` is never exercised. The only test passes text containing `. `, so the branch that returns the whole string when no sentence terminator is found has no coverage and could regress silently.

```rust
        Some(end) => text[..end + 1].to_string(),
        None => text.to_string(),
```
findings.title: Cover the no-terminator branch of first_sentence

value.summary: The new `summarise` module has four tests that assert real behaviour: truncation on word boundaries, the multibyte-panic regression, and first-sentence extraction. Two `None` branches — the no-space case in `shorten` and the no-terminator case in `first_sentence` — have no coverage and could regress silently. The deployment and compose changes are configuration/infra with no testable library behaviour.
